items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: In the orchestra was Byas, James Moody, Hubert Fol, Nat Peck, an American white trombonist...

ctx.x: I was so happy about being in France that I celebrated every day with a fresh bottle of cognac which I kept in my room and was drinking 15 to 20 glasses of cognac in bars and sidewalke cafes. But after a few weeks, my lips began to get dry and I could not play the way I was supposed to. I knew that it was from drinking too much, and although I was never drunk, I knew I had to stop drinking until my lips became right, and I did stop for at least one month.

Kenny Clarke who had been working in the orchestra of Tony Proto, a french altoist, and Lobo Nochio, a singer, formed an orchestra, and I joined it. Lobo had been in the army, was dischraged in Europe and had settled in Paris. In the orchestra was Byas, James Moody, Hubert Fol, Nat Peck, an American white trombonist, Jay Cameron, another white American, who played baritone sax, Pierre Michelot, a fine French bass player, and a few more French musieians whose names I don't remember. An English girl named Anabella…

We were engaged to work at Frisco's International Bopera House in Montmartre on rue Notre Dame de Lorette. I became acquainted with Frisco in 35. At one time, he had a club in London and had come to France in the 20's. I was not supposed to stay with the orchestra very long because I had been engaged before to go to Nice for two weeks in a place called Club St. Germain des Mers, which was to open in late July by Sarge Griffin and the director of the Edouard 7th theatre.
